content.text:
I submitted **holistic** with confidence 0.9, after spending 26 of the 60 budget.

**Design:** I trained the learner on L1-S1-M1 and L3-S2-M3. Then I tested two tasks chosen so the two hypotheses predict opposite results:
- **X = L3-S1-M1:** all three of its rules had already been trained, but its overall mapping matches the trained tasks on 0% of inputs.
- **Y = L2-S4-M2:** all three of its rules were new, but its mapping matches L1-S1-M1 on 56% of inputs.

A part-based learner should find X much easier than Y. A holistic learner should find Y easier.

**Results:** lower numbers mean faster learning.

| Task | Before training (3 tests) | After training (10 tests) |
|---|---|---|
| X (known rules, dissimilar) | mean about 61 | mean 42 (range 14–67) |
| Y (new rules, similar) | mean about 39 | mean 21.5 (range 5–41) |

After training, Y took about half as many examples as X. The test results are very noisy and the two ranges overlap. Still, Y came out lower in most samples, and the size of the gap is the opposite of what a part-based learner predicts. That is why I reported 0.9 confidence rather than higher.
